name: response_decode
summary: The response body could not be decoded to the bytes a reducer would parse.
trigger: The content-encoding decode of the response body failed.
grounding: Same policy and same class as request_decode, one side over: the rule lives in fixtures/content-encoding/ and this reason is what a turn carries when that rule refuses it. Reducers parse textual SSE and JSON, so a coding left undone yields silently empty content on the streaming path and a parse error on the one-shot path — both far from the cause. Erroring under a distinct reason is what puts it in a dashboard rather than in reducer_error.
not_expressible: As with request_decode, the decision is already executable one layer down over (body, encoding) pairs.
notes: This reason collapses the three failure classes the decode corpus keeps apart (unsupported, oversize, undecodable) into one label. That is a deliberate separate decision at this layer, not an oversight; splitting it is cheap because the classes are already named and asserted there. A truncated-but-salvageable response is NOT this reason — it decodes, is dispatched, and is metered as salvaged.
